newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Aokam near buying Idris assets.
newsitem.headline: Aokam near buying Idris assets.

text.p: Malaysia's Aokam Perdana Bhd said on Monday it was in the final stages of negotiations to buy two timber concessions and sawmills from Idris Hydraulic (M) Bhd.
In a statement, Aokam said the concessions and sawmills located in Malaysia's eastern Sabah state will cost about 400 million ringgit.
Aokam said it was also proposing a one-for-two rights issue at about 3.0 ringgit a share.
The stock of the timber company closed Monday trading at 5.60 ringgit, down 25 cents.

The concessions in the Sagissan area totalled about 176,388 hectares. Aokam officials said that under new terms of the concessions, the holder will be granted the rights to extract timber for 100 years.
Based on the present estimate, the projected total millable timber of the concession is about 40 million cubic metres during the concession period, they said.
Aokam's managing director Moehamad Izat Emir said the deal is expected to be completed in a few months' time.
The assets will be paid for by the issue of new Aokam shares and/or in cash, company officials said.
The rights issue will raise 324 million ringgit. It will be used as working capital, expenditure for product development, repayment of borrowings and other fixed financing obligations.

Aokam directors said they were confident that the proposed corporate exercise coupled with continuous internal development and restructuring exercise will contribute significantly to improvements in operational and financial performance of the group.
Aokam executive director Ng Chin Hoo said the new timber assets should start contributing to Aokam's bottomline in the next financial year ending June 30, 1998.
Aokam reported a net loss of 144.73 million ringgit in the year ended June 30, 1996, on the back of weak timber prices and insufficient log supply.
Aokam officials declined to comment on who is now the major shareholder of the company.
Former managing director Teh Soon Seng was reported to have sold his stake in Aokam. He resigned from the company early this month.
Aokam's 1995 annual report showed that Teh was its substantial shareholder with a 17.85 percent stake.
Aokam shares were actively traded in recent weeks on speculation of shareholding changes and asset injection. The stock closed on Monday at 5.60 ringgit, down 25 cents.
